newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen hovering after initial rise.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen hovering after initial rise.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to open higher on Friday, cheered by the Dow industrials' record rally overnight, but any climb in Tokyo's key index in the morning could fizzle later, brokers said.

They said major investors have been absent recently due to a lack of confidence of Japan's economic recovery and that has discouraged the market. The yen's slight advance against the dollar might also hurt market sentiment, they said.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed down 75.01 points or 0.37 percent at 20,121.41. Its September futures fell 50 to 20.170.
"The New York stocks hit a record high, but the Tokyo market lacks the energy to follow that trend," said a broker at a second-tier Japanese securities house.
A broker at another second-tier securities house said: "The Nikkei 225 should open higher, but we're not sure if it can remain up by the close because sentiment has been not good recently."
On Thursday, the Dow industrials soared 100.43 points to close at 7,895.81, the blue-chip average's first new high in nearly two weeks.
